Pre-Course Essential Vocabulary
Society - A broad community or nation living under a shared social order, government, and cultural expectations.
Norms - an accepted standard, pattern, or unwritten rule that guides behavior and defines what is usual, appropriate, or expected within a group or society.
Social Institutions - Organized systems of belief, behaviors, rules and relationships that structure social life.
Beliefs -Accepting that something is true, often without absolute proof or direct evidence.
Traditions -A belief, custom or way of behaving that has been passed down from generations.
Values - A culture’s deep, shared standards for is determined to be “good, right, fair and just”
Culture - ?????

What is Sociology: Definition
‘Sociology is the study of human social life, groups, social institutions and societies.

The focus of Sociology is on the influences from society which shape the behaviour of people, their experiences and their interpretations of the world around them.

Social Structures: The Building Blocks of Society

The Social Institutions and Social Relationships which form the building blocks of society

Sociology tries to understand how these various social institutions operate and how they relate to one another: Example: How Family may influence how well children perform in school


Sociology tries to explain the patterns of inequality and conflict within society

units.label: slide 14
units.text:
Sociology and Common Sense

Sociology looks at things which people already have knowledge of, simply by being alive people are aware of Religion, Family, etc

This leads people to believe that what sociologists study is just common sense (everyone already knows that)!

The idea that disease targets people at random, that men are superior to woman, that the poor are lazy, were all, and some are still, common sense views.

units.label: slide 15
units.text:
Common Sense
In some societies, it is considered normal for men to have many wives

In our society, we no longer burn witches when crops fail

However, some common sense views are the result of sociological research: Being poor makes it hard to succeed, social ties prevent loneliness

units.label: slide 16
units.text:
Sociology is different from common sense: Sociological Imagination
Sociologists use a Sociological Imagination (Mills) by asking if things really are as normal (common sense wise) as they seem, how things were in the past, how they’ve changed and how they differ across various cultures.

Sociologists look at evidence before they decide on something

Sociologists should maintain objectivity and value freedom (keeping an open mind) and suppressing personal belief.

In-Class Homework (Turn In When Finished)
You will be given a handout with 4 random scenarios. Each pair will have different scenarios so don't share answers with others. 
Decide and write what the common sense reaction would be for each scenario. Write it down. 
Ask yourselves..What else could be going on? Think of at least two variables that could explain the behavior. Write down two for each.
In the last part of class, share aloud at least 1 scenario and what you discussed.
Show me your finished written work for a homework grade.
For example: 
Scenario: Vašek doesnt speak in class.
Common Sense: Vašek is antisocial. Vašek is unintelligent.
Predict. What else is going on? Past experience. Vašek might feel uncomfortable with authority because of past experience. Friends/Peers. Vašek might be discouraged because he is afraid of looking “stupid” or “appearing to show off.”
